title: Table tennis and ATTP
excerpt: A message from ATTP on the role the association takes on in Moldovan sport, for players of every age and level.
body_html:
Table tennis and ATTP.

Playing table tennis teaches us that the game is not an end but a means. In performance sport, it is a means of competing and finding out who is strongest; among amateurs, it is a means of getting satisfaction and a chance to connect with other good and respectable people.

If ATTP gives even one person the chance to find their place in this sport, we can say with certainty that ATTP was not created in vain.

Here, however, we should make a small digression before saying what kind of means the game of table tennis is.

When our lads took part in the open competitions in Albena (Bulgaria) last summer and simply beat everyone there, we felt indescribable pride and joy for our players and for Moldovan sport as a whole. It is not as hopeless as our detractors would like it to be.

Even so, it is sad to admit that, apart from the results of our well-known veterans and players based abroad, we have had little to celebrate in recent years when it comes to our young players’ performances at international tournaments.

We have to give this example because it is highly relevant and topical.

The point here is not just resentment towards the country and the Federation. It is a matter of choice — the choice parents make for their children, the choice mentors and coaches make for their pupils, and the choice young people themselves make about which sport to play. And without a good reputation, the right conditions and appeal, we cannot talk about a secure, successful future for a sport like table tennis.

Attracting young people to table tennis is one of ATTP’s main goals.

As circumstances and everyday reality show, many of our talented young players who love table tennis (as Sofia Polcanova, Andrei Puțuntica, Vlad Ursu and Evghenii Dadechin were in their time) are not a thing of the past at all — it is simply that people often choose not to notice them, especially if they come from less well-off families. And what matters is not so much whether these young players become champions, but that they become happy, life-loving people of good faith.

As for the purpose of the “Federation”, since we have mentioned it... One of ATTP’s aims is to protect the interests of table tennis players wherever they are, whatever their age and playing experience. By showing attention and care for seniors and veterans, we set a good example for the younger generation, teaching them respect and mutual support, team spirit and trust.

ATTP is an opportunity to unite all Moldovan table tennis players into a real force and a healthy sporting community.

Thank you all, and every success going forward!
